name: Sossusvlei
imageAlt: Illustration of red sand dunes under a warm morning sky
description: A salt-and-clay pan ringed by some of the tallest dunes on Earth, deep inside the Namib-Naukluft National Park. Some dunes rise more than 300 metres, and the sand glows orange at sunrise.
tip: Enter the park gate at opening time so you reach the dunes before the midday heat.

name: Deadvlei
imageAlt: Illustration of dead trees on a pale clay pan beneath tall dunes
description: A white clay pan dotted with blackened, long-dead camelthorn trees against towering orange dunes. The trees have been preserved by the dry desert air for centuries.
tip: Carry plenty of water; there is no shade on the pan and the walk in is over soft sand.

name: Etosha National Park
imageAlt: Illustration of an acacia tree and a waterhole on open savanna
description: Namibia's flagship game reserve, built around a huge salt pan. In the dry season, elephants, lions, giraffes, zebras and rhinos gather at floodlit waterholes.
tip: Stay at a camp with a floodlit waterhole to watch animals at night.

name: Fish River Canyon
imageAlt: Illustration of a deep rocky canyon with a winding river at the bottom
description: One of the largest canyons in the world, roughly 160 kilometres long and up to about 550 metres deep. The main viewpoint at Hobas looks over the great bend of the river.
tip: The famous five-day hiking trail is only open in the cooler months and needs advance booking.

name: Skeleton Coast
imageAlt: Illustration of a ship wreck resting on a foggy desert shoreline
description: A remote, fog-wrapped coastline where the Namib Desert meets the cold Atlantic. Shipwrecks, whale bones and strong currents gave the area its name.
tip: Access to the northern park is limited, so book a permit or a guided trip well ahead.

name: Swakopmund
imageAlt: Illustration of a seaside town with a jetty and rolling waves
description: A relaxed seaside town with German colonial architecture and the adventure-sports capital of Namibia. Sandboarding, skydiving and quad biking are all within minutes of the centre.
tip: Mornings are often cool and foggy, so pack a jacket even in summer.

name: Walvis Bay
imageAlt: Illustration of pink flamingos wading in a calm lagoon
description: A working port city beside a sheltered lagoon that attracts thousands of flamingos and pelicans. Boat trips offer sightings of seals, dolphins and sometimes whales.
tip: Book a morning boat cruise when the water is calmest.

name: Spitzkoppe
imageAlt: Illustration of jagged granite peaks rising from a flat plain
description: A cluster of bald granite peaks rising from the desert plain, often called the Matterhorn of Namibia. Natural arches, rock pools and old rock paintings are scattered between the boulders.
tip: Camp on site; the dark skies make it one of the best stargazing spots in the country.

name: Twyfelfontein
imageAlt: Illustration of sandstone boulders carved with animal engravings
description: One of the largest concentrations of ancient rock engravings in Africa, recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007. The carvings show giraffes, rhinos, elephants and other animals.
tip: Hire the local guide at the visitor centre; they explain the meaning of the engravings.

name: Kolmanskop
imageAlt: Illustration of an abandoned house half filled with drifting sand
description: A former diamond-mining town near Lüderitz that was abandoned in the 1950s. The desert is slowly reclaiming the houses, filling rooms with drifting sand.
tip: Join the early guided tour for the best light and fewer visitors.

name: Lüderitz
imageAlt: Illustration of colourful harbour houses beside a rocky bay
description: A windswept harbour town with colourful colonial buildings, set between the desert and the Atlantic. It is known for fresh oysters and for the rugged coastline of the surrounding peninsula.
tip: Order local oysters at the waterfront, and expect strong afternoon winds.

name: Cape Cross Seal Reserve
imageAlt: Illustration of seals resting on a rocky shore
description: Home to one of the largest breeding colonies of Cape fur seals in the world, with tens of thousands of animals on the shore. Pups are born in November and December.
tip: Expect a strong smell and plenty of noise; the viewing walkway keeps you at a safe distance.

name: Waterberg Plateau Park
imageAlt: Illustration of a flat-topped red sandstone plateau above green bush
description: A rust-coloured sandstone plateau rising above the surrounding bushveld, protected as a sanctuary for rare and endangered species. White and black rhinos have been relocated here.
tip: Hike the guided trail to the plateau top for views across the plains.

name: Popa Falls
imageAlt: Illustration of a broad river tumbling over low rapids among green trees
description: A series of gentle rapids on the Okavango River in the green north-east of Namibia. The area is a quiet base for birdwatching and exploring Kavango culture.
tip: Visit after the rains, when the river runs fuller and the vegetation is lush.

name: Epupa Falls
activity: Waterfall walks and Himba village visits
imageAlt: Illustration of waterfalls cascading between palm trees on a river
description: A string of waterfalls on the Kunene River on the border with Angola, framed by fan palms and baobab trees. The surrounding area is home to the Himba people.
tip: Arrange village visits through a local guide to ensure respectful, consent-based visits.

name: Quiver Tree Forest
imageAlt: Illustration of branching quiver trees on a rocky plain at sunset
description: A natural stand of quiver trees (kokerboom) growing among dolerite rock formations near Keetmanshoop. The trees are a type of aloe, named after the San practice of making quivers from their branches.
tip: Arrive an hour before sunset to see the trees against the golden sky.

name: Windhoek
imageAlt: Illustration of a hillside city skyline with a church tower
description: Namibia's capital sits in the central highlands and is the gateway for most journeys into the country. It mixes colonial landmarks, craft markets, museums and a lively food scene.
tip: Use the city as a base to stock up on supplies before heading into remote areas.

name: Brandberg Massif
imageAlt: Illustration of a large granite mountain glowing red in the evening light
description: A huge granite mountain whose highest peak, Königstein, is the tallest point in Namibia at 2,573 metres. Thousands of ancient rock paintings are hidden in its gorges.
tip: Hiking here requires a registered local guide, so arrange one at the nearest community office.
